title: Home Rule League Movement 1916
definition: The Home Rule League Movement was the Indian response to the First World War, mirroring the Irish Home Rule movement, demanding self-government or 'Home Rule' within the British Empire through a two-league institutional setup led by Tilak and Annie Besant.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for Modern Indian History (GS-1). Frequently tested in Prelims (chronology, founders, distinct operational areas) and Mains (transition from moderate-extremist split to Lucknow Pact, shift in nationalist mobilization methods).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Home Rule League Movement 1916.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Rise of Extremism and Surat Split 1907
World War I impact on Indian National Movement
